decisions.reason: The polymer concrete drain housing remains close to the firm's core drainage engineering and likely serves as a durable platform component across system sales, so it should stay in the range despite some portfolio-pruning risk.
A floor-level shower drainage system is directly aligned with the firm's push toward accessible, low-profile bathroom solutions and is therefore unlikely to be withdrawn.
As the design-led flagship shower drainage line, it fits the firm's strategic positioning exceptionally well and should continue to be supported.

The backflow-protected basement floor drain addresses a real specialist problem and supports the firm's technical reputation, although its niche character makes it somewhat more vulnerable than the main shower lines.

The air-admittance valve is the least distinctive and least central to the firm's visible strategic focus on integrated bathroom drainage systems, so resources are better concentrated on core drainage products and new development.
